topic: Coca-Cola mailed millions of Americans a coupon for one free glass of Coke in the 1890s-1900s to build the habit nationwide
title: Coca-Cola Mailed Free Coke Coupons to Millions of Strangers
note: Gemini first draft, NOT fact-checked. Claude must verify every claim with its own 2-source rule before using any of it in a real job file.
draft_script: Coca-Cola's biggest trick wasn't its secret formula. It was a free drink. From the 1890s into the early 1900s, Coca-Cola mailed millions of Americans a coupon. Not for a discount. For one free glass of Coke. No strings attached. This wasn't about goodwill. It was a cold, calculated business move. The goal was simple: create a habit, nationwide. Get people to try it. Get them hooked. Permanently. Between 1894 and 1913, Coca-Cola issued 8.5 million of these free coupons. Imagine that scale. An estimated one in ten Americans received one. The redemption rate was incredibly high, around 85 percent. That's over 7 million free Cokes given away. Each free glass was an investment. Not in a single sale, but in a lifelong customer. This simple, massive giveaway built Coca-Cola's early customer base. It engineered demand. Free today, pay tomorrow. For decades. This is how Coca-Cola dominated the American market. A truly sneaky deal, perfectly executed to create an empire.
